q: Oxidation and reduction reactions involve the transfer of oxygen atoms, or hydrogen atoms, electrons, or change in ____.
e: Redox reactions can be defined through the transfer of oxygen, hydrogen, electrons, or changes in oxidation states.

q: When a substance gains oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is ____.
e: The addition of oxygen to a substance is the classical definition of oxidation.

q: When a substance loses oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is ____.
e: The removal of oxygen from a substance is the classical definition of reduction.

q: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is ____.
e: The removal of hydrogen (an electropositive element) from a substance is considered oxidation.

q: When a substance gains hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is ____.
e: The addition of hydrogen (an electropositive element) to a substance is considered reduction.

q: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or ____ element) to a substance.
e: The concept of oxidation is extended to include the addition of any electronegative element.

q: Reduction is the ____ of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance.
e: Reduction involves the removal of oxygen or any electronegative element from a substance.

q: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or ____ element) from a substance.
e: Oxidation can also be defined as the removal of hydrogen or any electropositive element.

q: Oxidation is the ____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: In terms of electron transfer, oxidation is defined as the loss of electrons.

q: Reduction is the ____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: In terms of electron transfer, reduction is defined as the gain of electrons.

q: Any element which increases in oxidation number is said to be ____.
e: An increase in oxidation number indicates a loss of electrons, which is oxidation.

q: Any element which decreases in oxidation number is said to be ____.
e: A decrease in oxidation number indicates a gain of electrons, which is reduction.
